page: Microsoft Azure L16aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Laosv4 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical AMD EPYC 9V74 cores running at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It includes a substantial local storage capacity of 11519 GB and is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25 percent. Text processing performance is also strong. However, multi-core operations, database operations, and memory write bandwidth fall into the average tier. A notable performance bottleneck is the uncached read-only memory bandwidth for large blocks, which registers in the bottom 25 percent at 36.77 GB/sec. Large-scale LLM inference is also a weak point, with the 70B model prompt processing speed falling into the bottom 10 percent.

Given the massive 11.5 TB local storage capacity and 128 GB of RAM, this server offers high resource density for storage-heavy and memory-intensive workloads without the added cost of external storage attachments. The hardware profile is highly suited for large-scale database hosting, data warehousing, and local file processing. It is less optimal for memory-bandwidth-bound applications or large-scale LLM inference due to the noted performance tradeoffs in those areas.
description: Microsoft Azure L16aos_v4 is a storage and memory-focused virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs, 128.0 GB of RAM, and a massive 11519 GB of local storage. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 server supports AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerations. Benchmarks reveal strong single-core CPU and text processing performance, though multi-core execution and database operations remain average. A key tradeoff is its uncached large-block memory read bandwidth, which performs in the bottom 25 percent. With its high local storage capacity and 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is highly suited for database hosting, large-scale data processing, and storage-intensive workloads where local high-capacity disk access is critical, while avoiding the overhead of external storage.
